findings.reason: the write sites and the write-path list must name `review_records.store_committed_review` (or its promotion caller) and `record_response`, or the index is stale by construction on the only store it indexes.
findings.text: the section hooks the wrong writers: `store_code_review` (`plan_review.py:5389`) writes `code_review_path(...)`, a `code-<neighbourhood>.json` in the crew-home store; `store_plan_review` (`:719`) writes through `_target_path(...)`, the same staging root; `store_portfolio_review` (`:6127`) likewise. None of the three writes the committed reviews tree the index covers — that tree is written at promotion through `store_committed_review` (`reckon/crew/review_records.py:168`, called from `reckon/crew/promotion.py:1809`) and rewritten in place by `record_response` (`plan_review.py:2338-2348`), and `review_records.py` and `promotion.py` are not in the section's write paths — so a worker building it as written adds index updates that never fire for the records a dispatch reads, and the whole saving falls back to the mismatch rebuild the section exists to remove

findings.reason: the section must name the index's path and add its writer to the write paths, and must say whether it covers the code-review store too, or the worker has to invent both.
findings.text: one index is placed "beside the committed review store" while its named updaters write a second store: committed plan-review records live in the tracked tree `docs/state/<project>/reviews/plan/<slug>/*.json` (1,995 files in 126 plan directories on this checkout, all in `git ls-files`), where a mutable index is untracked dirt in the shared checkout and in every worker worktree and readable by any broad `git add docs/…`, whereas the project's existing persisted store index for the sibling store is node-local by construction (`review_records._index_cache_path` → `node_local_cache_dir(directory.name)`, `review_records.py:1040-1048`); and the code-review half of `findings_by_path` reads yet another root, the crew home, through `list_code_reviews` (`findings.py:399-410`), which no index beside the committed store can cover

findings.reason: without a case that answers a finding on an indexed record and reads again, the section's own bar can pass while its most consequential stale-read path is unguarded, and the fix (validity per file stat identity, not per directory) belongs in the deliverable.
findings.text: the three cases and their control never cover an in-place rewrite of a record the index already holds: a committed record is rewritten in place, keeping its name and inode, whenever a finding is answered (`plan_review.record_response`, `plan_review.py:2338-2348`; the checkout currently shows ten such records modified), and `_open_findings_for` filters rows on `row.get("disposition") == "open"` (`plan_review.py:5129-5135`), so rows served from a stale entry would report an answered finding as open to the next dispatch
